status: v2 (22 Nov 2026): clusters, summaries, numbers. Draft: Aditya reviews.
setting: Invented materials (alloys, coatings, compounds) studied in invented lab studies. Properties and test methods are real concepts; material names, labs and findings are invented.

words.paper_kind: a critical review in materials science
words.source_kinds: lab studies and the materials and earlier studies they assess

parts.type: the type of material in one plain word, e.g. alloy, coating, polymer, ceramic

attrs.summary: a plasma-sprayed yttria-stabilised zirconia top coat on a nickel bond coat

study.about: an invented lab study, named by its lab and year

attrs.summary: dry sliding against an alumina ball at room temperature; wear volume measured by profilometry

reports_improvement.meaning: the study reports that the material improved the property it tested

reports_no_change.meaning: the study reports no clear change in the tested property for the material

reports_degradation.meaning: the study reports that the material worsened the tested property

fails_to_replicate.meaning: the study repeated an earlier study and did not get its result

confusable_note: DRAFT for review: for a property where lower is better (wear, creep) a fall is an improvement; small changes are written as improvement or as no change.
real_names_note: Real names that invented entities must not use (whole words, any case; world.check). Empty until Aditya approves the sources for this list.

questions.text: Which materials improved the tested property in {s}?
Which studies found that {o} improved the tested property, and which did not?

world_notes: Make 3-4 invented materials in the cluster's family and enough studies (years 2012-2025) that each paper has its own mix. A study may only fail to replicate an EARLIER study. Plant disagreements: two studies with opposite findings for the same material.
cluster_note: All materials and studies of this cluster belong to ONE material family within the cluster topic, and the studies test properties that matter for it.

effect.name: change in the tested property relative to the reference (%, positive = better)
